- **self**: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research (24/3)

## Structure and components

- [statement] Mark and Weber report that even a constant-rate exponential Hawkes likelihood can be multimodal, and propose a branching-structure EM method to improve convergence. Optimisation convergence and causal observation ordering are separate requirements; this EM result alone is not evidence of a latent drifting-background filter. (low confidence) — https://journals.aps.org/pre/pdf/10.1103/PhysRevE.101.043305 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] The Markov-modulated forward transition explicitly conditions on no arrivals between event times. Its live decoder also updates when no event occurs, so implementing only event-triggered updates would omit part of this documented algorithm. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.04027v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research

## How it works

- [statement] Santitissadeekorn’s negative-binomial extension explicitly targets a discrete-time excitation matrix and reconstructs no within-bin event times or continuous-time intensity path. Its application estimates the deterministic seasonal cycle offline. That application does not establish online latent-background filtering. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22742v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] The negative-binomial paper connects parameter-ensemble collapse to loss of adaptability: when parameter spread vanishes, regression increments shrink, and the parameter forecast must restore spread before the update can move again. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22742v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Santitissadeekorn, Delahaies and Lloyd provide a concrete causal count-data update: forecast from the previous intensity, parameter ensemble and observed counts; assimilate the next count only when it arrives; then update parameters from the intensity innovation. The parameter vector includes baseline, decay and excitation coefficients. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2302.00647v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Fabre and Muni Toke recommend log densities because tiny transition products can numerically collapse Viterbi scores to zero. This is a numerical safeguard for live regime inference. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.04027v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Omi, Hirata and Aihara explicitly reject their time-dependent-background smoother for online estimation because it uses surrounding observations. They require past-only data online and suggest a non-Gaussian state-space model; Kitagawa supplies a general recursive state-space framework, rather than a Hawkes-specific trading validation. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1702.04443v4 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research · also: https://www.jstor.org/stable/2289375
- [statement] Omi and colleagues find that an overly smooth background can inflate inferred branching ratios, and describe separation of endogenous and exogenous activity as difficult when background variation is unknown. Baseline adaptation and excitation learning therefore need to be assessed together rather than treating a burst as proof of increased excitation. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1702.04443v4 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Yang and colleagues provide online likelihood-based parameter learning: their algorithm observes an interval, updates the base-intensity estimate by a gradient step with a positive lower bound, and updates and projects triggering-function estimates. These are sequential parameter estimates, rather than a posterior filter for a latent drifting background process. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1801.08273v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] The negative-binomial paper warns that its factorised observation model omits contemporaneous dependence from shared latent drivers. A persistent common driver may be absorbed into estimated off-diagonal excitation, which limits background-versus-excitation interpretation. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22742v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] For count predictions, the negative-binomial paper uses the randomised probability integral transform and evaluates its mean and variance ratio. It uses the ensemble predictive mixture rather than a plug-in mean score so that forecast spread participates in the diagnostic. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22742v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Kitagawa illustrates a process-noise tradeoff: small Gaussian system noise can miss jumps, while large noise produces unwanted wiggle. Appropriate non-Gaussian system noise can represent abrupt and gradual changes; this example concerns general state-space smoothing rather than a Hawkes-specific online guarantee. (low confidence) — https://www.jstor.org/stable/2289375 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Their observation model uses Poisson counts and a discrete-time exponential-decay Hawkes recurrence with positive baseline, decay and excitation parameters. Their baseline is a model parameter estimated sequentially, rather than an independently specified latent background diffusion. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2302.00647v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Yang and colleagues describe a regularization tradeoff: stronger regularization improves algorithmic stability but changes the objective away from the negative log likelihood; weaker regularization reduces this distortion but can reduce stability. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1801.08273v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Kitagawa supplies general non-Gaussian state-space prediction, filtering and smoothing recursions and a numerical density approximation. This is methodological support for the state-space alternative cited by Omi; neither this abstract nor Omi supplies a fitted causal Hawkes background filter. (medium confidence) — https://www.jstor.org/stable/2289375 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research · also: https://arxiv.org/html/1702.04443v4
- [statement] Yang and colleagues’ theoretical setting assumes a constant bounded positive base intensity and bounded stationary increments. Its online learning guarantees must not be advertised as guarantees for arbitrary time-varying background rates. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1801.08273v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] The count-data ensemble method of Santitissadeekorn, Delahaies and Lloyd jointly estimates conditional intensity and model parameters. It first updates the intensity ensemble using Poisson–gamma conjugacy, then regresses intensity innovations onto the parameter ensemble. Its parameter vector includes baseline, decay and excitation strengths. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2302.00647v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Both sequential algorithms make the observation/update ordering explicit: Yang and colleagues observe an interval before updating parameters, while the count-data ensemble method waits for the next count before its analysis update. A completed-bin analysis estimate must be distinguished from a prediction made before that bin is observed. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1801.08273v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2302.00647v1
- [statement] The ensemble paper cautions that the parameter update is confined to the ensemble’s spanned subspace and is generally not optimal in the full parameter space. Small ensembles in high-dimensional problems can therefore miss update directions. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2302.00647v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] The ensemble Poisson-Gamma method updates the intensity ensemble using Poisson-gamma conjugacy and then regresses intensity innovations on the parameter ensemble. Ensemble spread approximates uncertainty; the parameter regression is not generally optimal in the full parameter space. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2302.00647v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Yang, Etesami, He and Kiyavash offer online gradient learning of both base intensity estimates and triggering functions. Each update follows observation of the completed interval. Their assumptions specify constant bounded base intensity and bounded stationary increments, so this result must not be presented as a guarantee for arbitrary drifting latent backgrounds. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/1801.08273v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Fabre and Muni Toke model a latent continuous-time Markov regime with a baseline and excitation kernel attached to each state. Their online Viterbi procedure produces a current optimal state without historical backward recursion; it is regime decoding, not a posterior mean estimate of a continuously drifting background. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.04027v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Fabre and Muni Toke separate parameter fitting from live state decoding: their EM expectation step defines both forward and backward likelihoods over the observation record, whereas their live algorithm starts with historical observations and advances on new events or intervals with no event. The published online decoder does not itself establish online EM parameter learning. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.04027v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
- [statement] Their goodness-of-fit section estimates intensity conditional on the full observation horizon and uses transformed inter-arrival durations with exponential QQ checks. This is a retrospective diagnostic and must not be substituted for evidence that a past-only background filter is calibrated. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.04027v1 · keywords: Causal online Hawkes background estimation for trading research
